tagline: Main street over the River Raisin, with Custer on the corner.
intro: M-125 is the old Dixie Highway, the auto trail meant to run from Chicago to Miami, and later US 25. Through Monroe it turns into Monroe Street and serves as the main street. Coming in from the north it passes St. Mary's, the oldest church in the county, crosses the River Raisin and runs down through the Old Village, the downtown platted in 1817.
Paper mills once lined the river. Before the mills came the War of 1812, and in January 1813, at the Battle of Frenchtown on the north bank, only 33 of General Winchester's 980 men escaped the field.

moments.title: Custer Equestrian Monument
moments.text: Custer's 14-foot bronze stood in mid-intersection in 1910, was moved off as a traffic hazard, and by 1955 sat so deep in brush that the movers could not find it.

moments.title: River Raisin National Battlefield Park
moments.text: East of downtown, on ground a paper mill held until 1995, lies the only national battlefield park for the War of 1812.

moments.title: Old Village
moments.text: South of the river the 1817 grid of numbered streets still holds the county courthouse, and the row buildings on Monroe Street keep shops below and apartments and offices above.
